info.name: Vybe Backend API
info.description:
Phase 1 + 2 API for the Vybe social app backend: auth (local + Google), user profiles (incl. profile photo upload), and posts (incl. image/video media upload).

**Before you start**
- Run the server locally (`npm run dev` inside `vybe_backend/`) against a MongoDB **replica set** — the app fails fast at boot otherwise (transactions require it).
- All variables (`base_url`, `access_token`, `userId`, etc.) are defined as **collection variables** with working defaults, so this collection runs correctly with NO environment selected at all — open the collection, check the "Variables" tab if you want to see/edit them directly. Selecting the "Vybe Backend - Local" environment is optional, only useful if you want a separate override (e.g. pointing `base_url` at staging) — when it IS selected, every script writes to both the environment and the collection variables together, so nothing gets shadowed or goes stale either way.
- `S3_BUCKET`/`AWS_REGION` must point at a real bucket your server's AWS credentials can write to for the media-upload requests (Upload Profile Photo, Create Post with Media, Edit Post - Replace Media) to succeed — everything else works without S3 at all.
- Auth endpoints are rate-limited (`AUTH_RATE_LIMIT_MAX` per `AUTH_RATE_LIMIT_WINDOW_MS`, default 10 requests / 15 min); upload endpoints have their own, separate, tighter limit (`UPLOAD_RATE_LIMIT_MAX`, default 30 / 15 min) — spamming either will eventually 429.
- Both `accessToken` and `refreshToken` are returned directly in the JSON response body (matching bepay's convention) — there is NO cookie involved anywhere in this API. The `refresh_token` variable is set automatically by Register/Login/Google Sign-In/Refresh's test scripts; Refresh and Logout send it back as `{ refreshToken }` in their own request bodies.
- Every response uses one consistent envelope: `{ success, data | error: { code, message, details }, timestamp }`.
- A collection-level pre-request script checks `base_url` before every send and throws a clear error if it's somehow still unresolved, instead of a confusing DNS/404 failure.

**Folders**
1. Auth — register/login/Google/refresh/logout
2. Users — profile read/update/search/profile-photo upload
3. Posts — create/edit/delete/read (text-only and with image/video media), with cursor pagination
4. Scenarios — demonstrates the backend's distinguishing behaviors: idempotent post creation, the ownership guard returning 404 (not 403) for another user's post, and private-account post gating.

request.description:
Creates a local account (argon2id password hash). `email`, `username`, and `googleId` each have a DB-level unique index — a duplicate returns `409 EMAIL_ALREADY_EXISTS` or `409 USERNAME_ALREADY_EXISTS`, translated from the raw Mongo duplicate-key error. `country` is optional, ISO 3166-1 alpha-2. The pre-request script mints a fresh unique username/email every send so this can be re-run without manual edits.

Both `accessToken` and `refreshToken` come back directly in the response body (no cookie) — the test script captures both into variables (collection scope always, environment too if one's selected). Also issues a UserStats(0,0,0) doc in the same transaction as the User doc.

request.description: Reuses the {{email}}/{{password}} set by Register's pre-request script. A wrong password and an unknown email both return the SAME `401 INVALID_CREDENTIALS` message (no user-enumeration signal). After `LOGIN_MAX_FAILED_ATTEMPTS` (default 5) consecutive failures the account locks for `LOGIN_LOCK_DURATION_MS` (default 15 min), returning `423 ACCOUNT_LOCKED` — a lock that has already expired grants a fresh attempt budget rather than instantly re-locking.

request.description:
Postman can't mint a real Google ID token — obtain one from your frontend's Google Sign-In flow (or Google's OAuth Playground against your own `GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID`) and paste it into the `google_id_token` variable before running this.

Server-side behavior worth knowing:
- Verifies the token's signature/issuer/audience/expiry via `google-auth-library`, and additionally requires `email_verified === true` (`401 GOOGLE_AUTH_FAILED` otherwise).
- If an existing local account already uses that email, this is REJECTED with `401 GOOGLE_AUTH_FAILED` rather than silently linked — auto-linking-by-email was identified as an account-takeover vector during review (an attacker could pre-register the victim's email locally) and deliberately removed. Log in with the local password instead.
- A brand-new Google user gets an auto-generated, collision-retried username derived from their display name.
- The response `user` object includes `googleId` (the provider's `sub` claim) whenever the account is Google-linked — omitted entirely for local-only accounts, matching bepay's `GlobalUserDTO` convention of only including provider ids when they actually exist.

request.description:
Sends back whatever `refresh_token` was captured by the last Register/Login/Google Sign-In/Refresh call. Rotates it (the old one is marked revoked server-side) and returns a fresh `accessToken` + a NEW `refreshToken` — the test script overwrites `refresh_token` with the new value, so re-running this request keeps working.

Replaying an already-rotated (or expired, or unknown) refresh token is treated as possible theft: the server revokes EVERY active refresh token for that user, forcing a full re-login on all devices, and returns `401 INVALID_REFRESH_TOKEN`. Omitting `refreshToken` entirely returns `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` instead (a missing-input error, distinct from an invalid one).

request.description: Revokes the given refresh token. Idempotent — `refreshToken` is optional here (unlike Refresh, where it's required): calling this with an empty body still returns 200, a deliberate no-op rather than an error.

Returns the caller's profile merged with their UserStats doc (followersCount/followingCount/postsCount), fetched in parallel via Promise.all — UserStats is a separate collection precisely so these counters don't live on (and contend with writes to) the User document itself. Requires `Authorization: Bearer {{access_token}}`.

Only `name`, `bio`, `country`, `isPrivate` are ever writable here — email/username changes are intentionally not supported by this endpoint (any other field sent is silently ignored, not an error). `profilePhotoUrl` is NOT settable here either — see "Upload Profile Photo" below; it's upload-only (no arbitrary client-supplied URL), closing off what would otherwise be an unvalidated external-URL input. Setting `isPrivate: true` immediately gates post visibility for everyone except you (see the Scenarios folder).

formdata.description: Required. PNG, JPEG, or WebP only.

request.description:
Select a PNG/JPEG/WebP file for the `photo` field before sending (required — omitting it returns `400 INVALID_PROFILE_PHOTO`).

Server-side behavior worth knowing:
- The file's actual bytes are verified against real PNG/JPEG/WebP magic-byte signatures — a renamed/mislabeled file (e.g. a `.txt` saved as `photo.png`) is rejected regardless of its extension or declared Content-Type (`400 INVALID_PROFILE_PHOTO`).
- Size is capped at `IMAGE_MAX_BYTES` (default 8 MB) — over that, `400 PROFILE_PHOTO_TOO_LARGE`.
- Upload ordering is deliberately sequential for safety: the NEW photo is uploaded and confirmed first, then `User.profilePhotoUrl` is updated (the only safe commit point), and only THEN is the OLD photo deleted from S3 (best-effort — a delete failure is logged, never fails the request). This ordering means a failed upload can never leave your profile pointing at a photo that doesn't exist, and a failed DB write never destroys a photo that was still your current one.
- This endpoint (along with post media uploads) has its own tighter rate limit (`UPLOAD_RATE_LIMIT_MAX`, default 30 / 15 min), separate from the general API limit, since a buffered upload holds its full file size in server memory for the request's duration.

Matches by username PREFIX (anchored regex — can use the unique username index) OR by a case-insensitive substring of `name`. Cursor-paginated: pass the last page's `nextCursor` as `cursor` for the next page. `q` is required, 1-50 chars.
Public profile fields only (no email). Returns `404 USER_NOT_FOUND` for an unknown or deactivated (`isActive: false`) username.

request.description:
This is the text-only path — plain JSON still works (multer simply no-ops when Content-Type isn't multipart, leaving express.json()'s parsed body untouched). `text` is required (1-500 chars). `clientRequestId` is an OPTIONAL client-generated idempotency key ({{$guid}} regenerates a fresh one on every send here) — a compound UNIQUE PARTIAL index on `(author, clientRequestId)` (only applied to documents where the field exists, so posts that omit it never collide) means retrying the exact same `clientRequestId` returns the ORIGINAL post with `200 OK` instead of creating a duplicate with `201 Created`. See "Replay Create Post" in Scenarios for a live demo. Also atomically increments the author's `UserStats.postsCount` inside the same transaction as the insert.

To attach an image or video, use "Create Post with Media" below instead — there's no `imageUrl` (or any other) field for supplying a pre-hosted URL; media only ever gets onto a post via upload.

request.description:
Same endpoint as "Create Post", but sent as `multipart/form-data` with a `media` file attached. Select an image OR a video for the `media` field before sending.

Server-side behavior worth knowing:
- The real `mediaType` is determined by sniffing the file's magic bytes (PNG/JPEG/WebP signatures, or an ISO-BMFF `ftyp` box / WebM EBML header for video) — never trusted from the file's extension or declared Content-Type.
- Size limits differ by the DETECTED type: images capped at `IMAGE_MAX_BYTES` (default 8 MB), video at the higher `VIDEO_MAX_BYTES` (default 50 MB) — an oversized image is still rejected (`400 POST_MEDIA_TOO_LARGE`) even though it's well under the video ceiling multer enforces first.
- The upload is sequenced BEFORE the post is created — a post is only ever created pointing at media that's already confirmed to exist in S3.
- Because `clientRequestId` is set, the S3 object key itself is DETERMINISTIC (`posts/{authorId}/{clientRequestId}.{ext}`): resending this exact request (e.g. after a timeout) overwrites the same key and returns the original post (`200`, unchanged `mediaUrl`) instead of creating a duplicate post or an orphaned second upload — see "2. Replay Create Post" in Scenarios for the same idea without media.

Author-only. The repository query combines `_id`, `author`, and `isDeleted: false` into ONE atomic filter — there is no separate "check ownership, then update" step. If the post doesn't exist OR belongs to someone else, this returns `404 POST_NOT_FOUND` either way (deliberately ambiguous, not `403`).

`text` alone is fine here (this request), but at least one of `text` or an attached `media` file is required — see "Edit Post - Replace Media" for attaching/replacing media, and note that sending neither returns `400 POST_VALIDATION_ERROR`.

formdata.description: Optional together with text below, but at least one is required.

request.description:
Same ownership guard as "Edit Post" (404 for not-found-or-not-yours) — checked BEFORE any upload is attempted, so a stranger's request never wastes an S3 call. Select a new image or video for `media` and send.

Server-side ordering: the new file is uploaded and confirmed first, then the post's `mediaUrl`/`mediaType` are updated (the safe commit point), and only THEN is the PREVIOUS media object deleted from S3 (best-effort, logged on failure, never blocks the response). Editing `text` only (no `media` field at all, as in the plain "Edit Post" request) leaves existing media completely untouched — nothing is re-uploaded or deleted.

Author-only, same combined-predicate guard as Edit. Soft-delete (`isDeleted: true`), not a hard delete — keeps referential integrity for likes/counters. Decrements `UserStats.postsCount` atomically in the same transaction.
Returns `404 POST_NOT_FOUND` if the post is soft-deleted, or if its author is private and you're not the owner (no Follow relationship exists yet in phase 1 — see Scenarios).

Cursor pagination on `_id` (reverse-chronological). Pass the previous page's `nextCursor` as `cursor` to continue. If the target account is private and you're not the owner, this returns `200 OK` with `{ isPrivate: true, isFollowing: false, posts: [] }` — a gated empty page, not an error — since "this account is private" is a normal UI state, not a failure.

request.description: Run this request TWICE in a row. First send: `201 Created`, a new post. Second send (same fixed `idempotency_key`, unlike the plain Create Post request which regenerates a fresh `{{$guid}}` every time): `200 OK` with the IDENTICAL post id, and `UserStats.postsCount` is not double-incremented. This is the `(author, clientRequestId)` partial unique index + catch-and-refetch pattern in action.

exec: pm.test('Status code is 404, not 403', function () { pm.response.to.have.status(404); });

request.description: Uses {{secondary_access_token}} to try editing a post owned by the PRIMARY user ({{postId}}). Returns 404, identical to what you'd get for a post that doesn't exist at all — the repository never distinguishes "not found" from "not yours" for mutations, by design.
Run this as the PRIMARY user (default {{access_token}}). Flips {{username}}'s account to private.
